strengths: Addresses a clear gap in online data curation for object detection with well-motivated problem statement and clear articulation of why existing methods fail

Principled technical approach using AP-based marginal contributions with rigorous mathematical formulation, elegant closed-form solution (O(1) per detection), and Monte Carlo verification of analytical correctness

Comprehensive experimental validation with consistent improvements (~2.0-2.7 mAP) across 6 diverse detector architectures (Faster R-CNN, ATSS, FCOS, VFNet, GFL, Deformable DETR) demonstrating broad applicability

Strong robustness under challenging conditions: noisy annotations (maintains superiority across 0-100% noise levels), pseudo-labels (+2.8 mAP), and combines effectively with knowledge distillation (+3.7 mAP combined gains)

Fully model-agnostic design operating at data pipeline level without modifying architectures, loss functions, or training procedures; enables straightforward integration into diverse codebase implementations

Thorough ablation studies systematically examining augmentation effects (Table 2), teacher capacity impact (Table 3), prior distribution stability (Figure 4, ρ≈0.94), and comprehensive comparison with alternative metrics (Table 4)

Excellent reproducibility with clear Algorithm 1, detailed implementation specs, extensive augmentation configurations (Table 9), verified on open-source MMDetection framework, and validation on additional datasets (VOC2007, BDD100K)
weaknesses: Uniform prior (Beta(1,1)) approximation lacks complete theoretical justification—while empirical ranking stability is demonstrated (ρ≈0.94), the claim that 'absolute values are approximate but ordering is stable' is hand-wavy; gap between uniform distribution and actual detector scores not thoroughly analyzed

First-order additivity assumption (Eq. 27) only empirically validated for one regime (64→16 super-batch, Figure 6); no theoretical analysis of breakdown conditions; independence of class-level score distributions across mAP averaging not justified

Teacher-student architectural coupling significantly limits flexibility: Table 6 shows substantial performance drops with cross-family teachers (38.6 vs. 39.9 mAP), and requirement for same-family teachers with larger backbones reduces generality

Strong data augmentation emerges as hidden critical dependency: Table 2 shows pure sampling overfits severely (50.3 train vs. 37.3 val); augmentation strategy is 'relatively naïve' (authors' admission); detector-family-specific tuning (Table 9) adds hyperparameter burden

Computational overhead is substantial (3× iteration time, Table 12: 0.25s→0.75s) despite practical gains; while dynamic selection ratio (Appendix 8) recovers performance with 30% time reduction, this critical optimization is relegated to appendix and adds complexity

Limited technical novelty: core teacher-student learnability concept directly from RHO-LOSS [38] and JEST [14]; main contribution is adapting existing framework to detection via AP-based scoring—somewhat incremental; closed-form solutions under uniform prior are routine mathematics

Moderate absolute improvements (~2.0-2.7 mAP on saturated COCO benchmark) comparable to standard architectural advances rather than transformative; improvements decrease significantly with longer schedules (Table 13: 6.7 mAP at 3× vs. 2.7 at 1×), raising convergence questions

Incomplete analysis of failure modes and performance variation: 1.6-3.1 mAP range across detectors (Table 1) with no systematic explanation; no exploration of when/why DetGain underperforms; VFNet (+2.2 mAP) vs. FCOS (+2.8 mAP) discrepancy unexplained

Image-level aggregation across 80 classes and 10 IoU thresholds (800 terms in Eq. 9) assumes independence; classes and thresholds exhibit correlations; equal class weighting ignores nuanced long-tail importance despite claims of automatic mitigation

Evaluation scope limited primarily to COCO with high-capacity models (ResNet-50 students); VOC/BDD100K results relegated to appendix with single runs and no error bars; unclear performance on lightweight backbones (MobileNet, EffecientNet) or extreme long-tail distributions
